blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Modern image restoration methods increasingly rely on large-scale supervised training, yet clean targets are often prohibitively difficult to obtain in scientific imaging modalities such as hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Plug-and-play ADMM (PnP-ADMM) with pretrained diffusion priors offers a promising alternative, but the learned prior distribution can mismatch both the target scientific image distribution and the distribution of ADMM denoiser inputs induced by dual feedback. To mitigate these mismatches, we propose $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP, a self-supervised plug-and-play restoration framework that learns a score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. Specifically, the learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-driven corrections with analytical regularization. We further analyze the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm assuming an ideal score and quadratic data fidelity. Experiments on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods.
blocks.zh: 现代图像恢复方法越来越依赖于大规模监督培训,然而,在超光谱成像(HSI)和磁共振成像(MRI)等科学成像模式中,清洁的目标往往难以获得。 PnP-ADMM(PnP-ADMMM)带有被预先训练的传播前科,提供了一个很有希望的替代方案,但事先获得的传播既可以不匹配目标科学图像的传播,又可以不匹配由双重反馈诱导的ADMM denoiser输入的传播. 为了缓解这些不匹配,我们提议$\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP,一个自我监督的插件和游戏恢复框架,它直接从观测衍生的ADMM中间状态中吸取分数,没有干净的训练目标或外部预先训练的分数. 具体而言,学到的分数纠正了对分析前更新的投入,将观察驱动的校正与分析正规化相结合。 我们进一步分析经过修正的ADMM算法的趋同与重建错误,假设是理想分数和四相数据忠实. 关于参考指导的HSI恢复、单图像HSI去诺和核磁共振去诺的实验表明,与相竞方法相比,持续改进。

blocks.en:
Diffusion-based PnP methods and ADMM variants often use diffusion models pretrained on natural RGB images ( Zhu et al., 2023 ; Wu et al., 2024 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Shrestha and Fu, 2026 ) . Figure 1 (a) illustrates how a pretrained diffusion model supplies the prior update within ADMM. Applying such priors to scientific imaging can introduce two distinct mismatches, illustrated in Figure 1 (b).
First, natural RGB images differ from scientific images in their image statistics and representations, creating a mismatch between the pretraining and target domains. Adapting these priors to modalities such as hyperspectral imaging and MRI may therefore require additional representation or model adaptation ( Pang et al., 2024 ; Xiao et al., 2025 ; Gao and Zhou, 2024 ) .
Second, even within the same modality, ADMM denoiser inputs need not follow the Gaussian perturbation distributions used to train score models, because they also reflect dual feedback and solver-dependent errors. AC–DC mitigates this mismatch by adapting solver inputs to a pretrained score model through noise injection and conditional Langevin correction ( Shrestha and Fu, 2026 ) . This motivates a complementary direction: learning score corrections directly from observation-derived ADMM states, so that their statistics inform the prior update without requiring an externally pretrained model.

blocks.en:
To address these mismatches in scientific image restoration, we introduce S 3 -PnP for settings without domain-matched pretrained priors. The framework learns a self-supervised score approximation at test time from ADMM denoiser inputs generated by the available observations. The learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-adapted state statistics with analytical regularization. Training requires neither clean targets nor externally pretrained weights. Under a matched quadratic denoising model with ideal score corrections, we establish sufficient conditions for convergence of the corrected ADMM iterations and lower expected reconstruction error relative to the matched analytical ADMM baseline. Because structured interference may enter the learned state statistics, a structure-guided learning strategy combines complementary orthogonal projections with sequential training. We evaluate S 3 -PnP on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising.
Our contributions are:

blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Plug-and-Play and Generative Priors for Image Restoration. PnP combines denoisers with observation-model updates ( Venkatakrishnan et al., 2013 ) , with subsequent analyses covering fixed-point convergence, Lipschitz conditions, and proximal denoiser constructions ( Chan et al., 2017 ; Ryu et al., 2019 ; Hurault et al., 2022 ) . For RGB restoration, DDRM uses spectral decompositions of linear observation operators ( Kawar et al., 2022 ) , while DDNM uses range–null-space decomposition to enforce data consistency ( Wang et al., 2023 ) .
DPS and Π \Pi GDM guide diffusion sampling through approximate measurement likelihoods ( Chung et al., 2023 ; Song et al., 2023 ) .
DiffPIR combines diffusion denoising with half-quadratic splitting ( Zhu et al., 2023 ) , and PnP-DM uses split Gibbs sampling for likelihood and prior updates ( Wu et al., 2024 ) .
PnP-Flow constructs time-dependent denoisers from pretrained flow-matching models ( Martin et al., 2025 ) , while CM4IR uses consistency models for few-step restoration ( Garber and Tirer, 2025 ) .
ADMMDiff coordinates generative priors and guidance within ADMM ( Zhang et al., 2025 ) . For non-RGB imaging, PLRDiff and HIR-Diff use low-dimensional spectral representations to apply pretrained three-channel diffusion priors to HSI restoration ( Rui et al., 2024 ; Pang et al., 2024 ) .
DM-ZS learns guidance and spectral mapping from PAN and low-resolution HSI observations for pansharpening with a pretrained RGB diffusion model ( Xiao et al., 2025 ) .
For MRI reconstruction, Chung and Ye (2022) combine an MRI-trained score prior with data-consistency updates, while DDS couples diffusion sampling with conjugate-gradient updates ( Chung et al., 2024 ) .
MRPD transfers a natural-image latent diffusion prior to MRI with optional autoencoder adaptation ( Gao and Zhou, 2024 ) , and PnP-CM incorporates MRI-trained consistency models into PnP-ADMM ( Gülle et al., 2026 ) . Our framework combines learned score corrections with an analytical prior update within ADMM.
The corrections act on the prior input, allowing learned information to complement analytical regularization.

blocks.en:
Self-Supervised Prior Learning and Adaptation. Self-supervised learning and prior adaptation address limited clean supervision and mismatch with the target restoration problem. Shoushtari et al. (2024) analyze denoiser mismatch in PnP-ADMM and investigate adaptation using target-domain samples.
AC–DC addresses the mismatch between pretrained score models and ADMM inputs shaped by dual feedback through Gaussian noise injection and conditional Langevin corrections ( Shrestha and Fu, 2026 ) .
To learn without clean targets, Noise2Self constructs self-supervised losses using noise independence and masked prediction ( Batson and Royer, 2019 ) .
For score estimation, DSM connects perturbation-based denoising regression to distribution scores ( Vincent, 2011 ) .
Noise2Score learns the score of the noisy-image distribution and uses Tweedie’s formula for restoration ( Kim and Ye, 2021 ) , while C2S introduces generalized denoising score matching on further-corrupted observations for MRI denoising ( Tu et al., 2025 ) .
Learning directly from the observations to be restored provides another route to reducing external data requirements.
ZS-N2N trains a lightweight network on downsampled pairs from a single noisy image ( Mansour and Heckel, 2023 ) , and DDS2M optimizes spatial and spectral networks during reverse diffusion using only the degraded HSI ( Miao et al., 2023 ) .
For diffusion MRI, DDM 2 combines statistical denoising with generative diffusion in a three-stage framework ( Xiang et al., 2023 ) ; Di-Fusion uses later diffusion steps and adaptive sampling in a single-stage self-supervised framework ( Wu et al., 2025 ) .
We learn score corrections at test time from ADMM states generated by the available observations.
These corrections modify the input to an analytical prior update, combining observation-driven learning with analytical regularization without externally pretrained weights.

blocks.en: 3.1 Self-Supervised Score Approximation from ADMM Iterates
blocks.zh: 3.1 ADMM的自我监督分数 迭代图

blocks.en: Analytical priors in ADMM capture structures such as low rank and sparsity, but may not fully describe the statistics of the denoiser inputs generated during optimization. These statistics can complement analytical regularization, helping suppress noise while preserving image content. Therefore, S 3 -PnP learns an implicit regularization correction from ADMM denoiser inputs generated by the current observations. We estimate this correction through self-supervised score regression without externally pretrained weights and apply it before the analytical prior update.
blocks.zh: ADMM捕捉结构中的分析前科,如低阶和相扑等,但可能无法充分描述优化期间产生的denoiser输入的统计. 这些统计可以补充分析规范化,帮助抑制噪音,同时保留图像内容. 因此,S 3-PnP从当前观测结果产生的ADMM denoiser输入中学习出一种隐含的正性校正. 我们通过自我监督的分数回归来估计这种校正,而无需经过外部预先训练的分数,并在分析前更新之前应用.

blocks.en:
Self-supervised score learning. Firstly, we run Eq. ( 2 ) with its analytical prior update and collect the denoiser inputs C k = A k + 1 + U k C^{k}=A^{k+1}+U^{k} into a training set ℬ \mathcal{B} to capture observation-dependent state statistics. Each state C ∈ ℬ C\in\mathcal{B} is normalized as Z = 𝒮 ⁡ ( C ) = ( C − m ) / s Z=\mathcal{S}(C)=(C-m)/s , using fixed medians m m and positive scales s s estimated from ℬ \mathcal{B} . Then, we construct the perturbed state Z t = Z + Δ t ​ ϵ Z_{t}=Z+\sqrt{\Delta_{t}}\epsilon , where ϵ ∼ 𝒩 ⁡ ( 0 , I ) \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I) is independent of Z Z and Δ t > 0 \Delta_{t}>0 is the artificial perturbation variance.
In order to formulate a correction direction from these state statistics, let p t p_{t} denote the density of Z t Z_{t} and define the state energy R t ​ ( z ) = − log ⁡ p t ​ ( z ) R_{t}(z)=-\log p_{t}(z) . The score of the perturbed state distribution is its log-density gradient, ∇ z ​ log ​ p t ​ ( z ) = − ∇ z R t ​ ( z ) \nabla_{z}\log p_{t}(z)=-\nabla_{z}R_{t}(z) , which provides a correction direction reflecting the reference-state statistics. Since p t p_{t} is unknown, we estimate this score through self-supervised regression using the collected states and their artificial perturbations. Specifically, we build on the regression principle of generalized denoising score matching (GDSM) ( Tu et al., 2025 ) . The following lemma establishes the relationship between its optimal restoration predictor and the state score, providing the basis for learning the required correction without clean training targets.

blocks.en: We evaluate S 3 -PnP on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising. The experiments include quantitative and qualitative comparisons, ablation studies, and controlled tests of the theoretical predictions.
blocks.zh: 我们评价S 3-PnP的参考指导HSI还原,单像HSI去诺,核磁共振去诺. 这些实验包括定量和定性的比较,衰减研究,以及理论预测的控制测试.

blocks.en: 4.1 Datasets and Experimental Settings
blocks.zh: 4.1 数据集和实验设置

blocks.en: Datasets and Experimental Settings. We evaluate reference-guided hyperspectral restoration on the Dongying dataset from HiPandas ( Xu et al., 2025 ) , using a noisy low-resolution HSI as input and a PAN image as guidance. For single-image hyperspectral denoising, we use Qingpu and Xiong’an, with a single noisy HSI as input. Both tasks are evaluated under Gaussian and mixed noise at varying intensity levels. MRI denoising is evaluated on BrainWeb at the official 3%, 5%, and 7% noise levels and on M4Raw using acquired noisy images from all 25 test subjects. For all learning-based methods without pretrained weights, self-supervised training is performed at test time using only the noisy test observations. Dataset and implementation details are provided in Appendix B.5 . We report PSNR and SSIM for all tasks, supplemented by SAM and ERGAS for both hyperspectral tasks; higher PSNR/SSIM and lower SAM/ERGAS indicate better performance.
blocks.zh: 数据集与实验设置. 我们评价HiPandas(Xu等,2025年)的Dongying数据集上的参考制导超光谱修复,使用噪音低分辨率HSI作为输入,并使用PAN图像作为取向。 对单相超光谱去诺, 我们使用清普和Xiong'an, 这两项任务在高斯因下评价,不同强度下混合出噪音. 核磁共振去诺在BrainWeb上通过正式的3%、5%和7%的噪音水平以及M4Raw上通过所有25个测试对象获得的噪音图像进行评估。 对于所有没有被预先训练的分量的以学习为基础的方法,在测试时只使用吵闹的测试观察进行自我监督训练. 数据集和执行细节见附录B.5。 我们对所有任务报告PSNR和SSIM,对超光谱任务的SAM和ERGAS加以补充;较高的PSNR/SSIM和较低的SAM/ERGAS显示性能更好.

blocks.en: Baselines. For reference-guided hyperspectral restoration, we follow the baseline setup of UHiPandas ( Xu et al., 2025 ) . Comparisons include UHiPandas and cascaded pipelines constructed from R-PNN ( Guarino et al., 2024 ) , HIR-Diff ( Pang et al., 2024 ) , PWRCTV ( Xu et al., 2024 ) , PLRDiff ( Rui et al., 2024 ) , and SwinIR ( Liang et al., 2021 ) . For single-image hyperspectral denoising, baselines include BM4D ( Maggioni et al., 2013 ) , HLRTF ( Luo et al., 2022 ) , RCTV ( Peng et al., 2022 ) , DDS2M ( Miao et al., 2023 ) , LRTFR ( Luo et al., 2024 ) , HIR-Diff ( Pang et al., 2024 ) , and CF-INR ( Yu et al., 2026 ) . For MRI denoising, baselines include Noise2Self ( Batson and Royer, 2019 ) , Noise2Void ( Krull et al., 2019 ) , Noisier2Noise ( Moran et al., 2020 ) , R2R ( Pang et al., 2021 ) , Noise2Score ( Kim and Ye, 2021 ) , ZS-N2N ( Mansour and Heckel, 2023 ) , C2S ( Tu et al., 2025 ) , and DRDD ( Lin et al., 2026 ) . In our comparisons, HIR-Diff, PLRDiff, and DRDD use pretrained diffusion weights, whereas DDS2M performs self-supervised learning during reverse diffusion and C2S trains a denoising predictor through generalized denoising score matching.
blocks.zh: 基线。 关于参考制导的超光谱恢复,我们遵循UhiPandas的基准设置(徐等,2025年)。 比较包括由R-PNN(Guarino等,2024年)所建造的UHiPanda和级联管,HIR-Diff(Pang等,2024年),PWRCTV(徐等,2024年),PLRdiff(Rui等,2024年)和SwinIR(梁等,2021年)等. 对于单相超光谱去诺,基线包括BM4D (Maggioni等,2013年),HLRTF (Luo等,2022年),RCTV (Peng等,2022年),DDS2M (Miao等,2023年),LRTFR (Lo等,2024年),HIR-Diff (Pang等,2024年),和CF-INR (Yu等,2026年). 对于核磁共振去诺,基线包括:Noise2Solis(Batson和Royer,2019年),Noise2Void(Krull等,2019年),Noisier2Noise(Moran等,2020年),R2R(Pang等,2021年),Noise2Score(Kim和Ye,2021年),ZS-N2N(Mansour和Heckel,2023年),C2S(Tu等,2025年)和DRD(Lin等,2026年). 在我们的比较中,HIR-Diff,PLRdiff,和DRDD使用被预先训练的传播权重,而DDS2M则在逆向扩散过程中进行自我监督的学习,而C2S则通过通用去诺分比来训练去诺能预测器.

blocks.en: 4.2 Quantitative and Qualitative Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 定量和定性结果

blocks.en: Quantitative comparisons. Tables 1 – 3 and Appendix C.2 summarize the results for the three restoration tasks. For reference-guided HSI restoration, S 3 -PnP achieves better average restoration performance than the compared cascaded methods and UHiPandas in both noise groups, with improved spectral fidelity under mixed noise. Similarly, for single-image HSI denoising on Qingpu, it outperforms the reported baselines under both Gaussian and mixed noise. For MRI denoising, S 3 -PnP achieves the best reported average performance at all three BrainWeb noise levels. On M4Raw, S 3 -PnP learns only at test time and achieves results comparable to pretrained C2S. S 3 -PnP generally outperforms the evaluated pretrained diffusion methods and the self-supervised diffusion method.
blocks.zh: 数量比较。 表1-3和附录C.2概述了三项修复任务的结果。 对于参考制导的HSI还原,S 3-PnP比两个噪声组中的相比较级联法和UHiPanda都实现了更好的平均还原性能,在混合噪声下光谱的忠度得到提高. 同样地,对于在清普上进行单相的HSI去名化,它在高斯和混合噪音下都超过了所报告的基线。 对于核磁共振去诺,S 3-PnP在所有三个BrainWeb噪声级别上都实现了所报最佳平均性能. 在M4Raw上,S 3-PnP只在测试时间学习并取得与预训C2S相当的结果. S 3 - PnP一般比被评价的事先训练的传播方法和自我监督的传播方法要好.

blocks.en: Qualitative comparisons. Figure 3 presents visual comparisons for the three restoration tasks. For reference-guided HSI restoration on Dongying, S 3 -PnP recovers clearer spatial boundaries and colors closer to the reference, while several cascaded methods exhibit color shifts or residual artifacts. For single-image HSI denoising on Qingpu, it suppresses noise while preserving fine spatial structures, whereas some competing methods leave visible noise or blur local details. On BrainWeb and M4Raw, it reduces noise while retaining tissue boundaries and local anatomical structures. The enlarged regions highlight these differences in noise suppression and detail preservation, and the error maps reveal the remaining discrepancies from the references.

We examine Theorem 1 using matched solvers with positive-definite quadratic fidelity and exact singular-value soft thresholding. Under wide-spectrum fidelity, the tested corrections accelerate the empirical decay of the normalized distance between trajectories from two initializations (Figure 5 (a)): at β = 1 \beta=1 , the distance reaches 10 − 10 10^{-10} in 44 iterations, compared with 93 for analytical ADMM. Some settings outside the sufficient contraction region still show decaying distances, whereas β = 4 , 8 \beta=4,8 , beyond the theorem’s range, produce growing distances (b).
Moderate corrections ( β = 0.25 , 0.5 \beta=0.25,0.5 ) reduce reconstruction error across the tested prior strengths, whereas stronger corrections can increase error under strong analytical regularization (c). Under near-matched fidelity, all eight sampled settings satisfying the improvement condition yield empirical gains above the positive theoretical lower bound (d), consistent with the predicted improvement and illustrating the bound’s conservatism. blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en: We presented S 3 -PnP, a self-supervised PnP-ADMM framework for scientific image restoration. By learning score corrections from ADMM states generated by the available observations, the framework connects prior learning to the restoration process. These corrections refine the inputs to analytical prior updates, complementing analytical regularization without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. We further analyzed the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm under ideal scores and quadratic data fidelity. Through task-specific observation models, the framework supports reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising. Our work provides a common approach to integrating observation-driven score learning with analytical optimization for scientific imaging.
blocks.zh: 我们提出了S 3-PnP,一个自我监督的PnP-ADMM科学图像修复框架. 通过学习从ADMM状态得到的由可用观测产生的分数校正,框架将之前的学习与恢复过程联系起来. 这些更正完善了对分析前更新的投入,补充了分析规范化,没有干净的培训目标或外部预先训练的权重。 我们进一步分析了经过修正的ADMM算法在理想分数和四相数据忠实性下的趋同与重建错误. 该框架通过针对特定任务的观测模型,支持以参考为指南的HSI还原,单像HSI去名,核磁共振去名. 我们的工作为将观测驱动分数学习与科学成像分析优化相结合提供了一个共同的方法。

blocks.en: Correction network. The correction network is a shallow conditional U-Net with feature widths 48 and 96, four residual blocks, and one downsampling–upsampling pair. Each residual block uses GroupNorm and SiLU activations and is conditioned on a 128-dimensional embedding of the perturbation level. The input concatenates the normalized state, a one-channel guide, and three scalar condition maps. The final convolution is zero-initialized. The state has r = 6 r=6 , 12 12 , and 1 1 channels for reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising, respectively. HiPandas uses the observed PAN image as guidance; HSI denoising and MRI use guidance derived from their noisy observations. Each network contains approximately 0.64 0.64 – 0.65 0.65 million trainable parameters, with the architecture and exact counts given in Table 4 . Dual-track inference uses two networks with the same architecture and independent weights, doubling the parameter count.

blocks.en: Training states. We first run the analytical ADMM solver and collect its denoiser inputs into a state bank ℬ 0 \mathcal{B}_{0} . For single-track learning, the correction network is trained directly on ℬ 0 \mathcal{B}_{0} . For dual-track learning, we first train the structure network on ℬ 0 \mathcal{B}_{0} and freeze its weights. We then run ADMM with the structure correction enabled to construct a second bank ℬ 1 \mathcal{B}_{1} , on which the complementary network is trained. This sequential procedure allows the complementary network to adapt to states generated after the structure correction. Each network is trained on a fixed bank without backpropagating through the ADMM iterations, and all network weights are fixed during final inference.

blocks.en:
Reference-guided HSI restoration. We use the Dongying dataset 1 1 1 https://github.com/shuangxu96/Hipandas from HiPandas ( Xu et al., 2025 ) . It contains 81 samples with 32 spectral bands. Each sample consists of a noisy 64 × 64 × 32 64\times 64\times 32 low-resolution HSI and a 256 × 256 256\times 256 PAN image, with a target HSI of size 256 × 256 × 32 256\times 256\times 32 . The spatial scale factor is four.
The Gaussian conditions include G10 and G30, as well as GNI
with band-dependent, non-i.i.d. Gaussian noise. The mixed conditions, Mix35, Mix55, and Mix55-G30, combine Gaussian noise with stripe and bad-line interference at different severity levels.
For each condition, all 81 noisy samples contribute states to a shared training bank, and the resulting network or network pair is shared across the samples. Training uses 64 × 64 64\times 64 crops in high-resolution state coordinates, corresponding to 16 × 16 16\times 16 low-resolution observation regions. Inference restores each complete sample. Clean high-resolution images are excluded from the training losses and are used for parameter selection and evaluation. Metrics are computed per sample and then averaged over all 81 samples.

Training uses crops of solver states generated from the noisy observations.
